original_question: If G is a pro-Lie group and G0 is its identity component, must the quotient group G/G0 be complete? Equivalently in the paper's discussion, is G/G0 always prodiscrete?
target_in_paper: Question 2 in Section 3: "Let G be a pro-Lie group with identity component G0. Is G/G0 complete (and therefore, prodiscrete)?" ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It uses the right class of groups (pro-Lie groups), the right subgroup (the identity component G0), the right quotient (G/G0), and the same property asked in the paper (completeness), while also matching the paper’s prodiscrete reformulation. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
missing_details: Say explicitly that this is an open problem in the paper, namely Question 2, not a theorem or conjecture proved there. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
Make the universal quantifier explicit: the question asks whether this holds for every pro-Lie group G. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

Define G0 stand-alone as the connected component of the identity in G. The paper uses the notation without re-explaining it in the question itself. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

Specify that G/G0 carries the quotient topology and that "complete" means complete as a topological group. The surrounding discussion is about completeness in the topological-group sense. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

If you keep the alternate wording, define "prodiscrete" stand-alone as a projective limit of discrete groups (equivalently, a closed subgroup of a product of discrete groups). In this context the paper’s reformulation is justified because complete quotients of pro-Lie groups are pro-Lie, and a pro-Lie group is prodiscrete iff it is totally disconnected; pro-Lie groups are complete. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

No ambient field, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency restrictions are part of this problem; the hidden assumptions are purely topological-group notions. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
refined_question: Open problem. For every pro-Lie group G, with G0 denoting the connected component of the identity and G/G0 equipped with the quotient topology, is the component group G/G0 complete as a topological group? Equivalently, is G/G0 always prodiscrete? ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: For every pro-Lie group G, is the component group G/G0 prodiscrete? ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
justification: This draft clearly targets the paper’s Question 2 in Section 3, which is stated immediately after Theorem 5 gives sufficient conditions for quotients G/N to be pro-Lie. The nearby context also records the Abelian positive case in Theorem 6(iii). Later, in Section 7, Theorem 13 is singled out precisely because it reduces this open problem to the case where the identity component is prosolvable. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is simply the stand-alone version of Question 2, with the quotient-topology and completeness terminology made explicit. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
